steps: Analgesia: an NSAID (e.g. IM/PR diclofenac) is first-line; opioid if NSAID contraindicated.
Antiemetic and fluids as needed; non-contrast CT KUB to confirm and size the stone.
Most stones <5 mm pass spontaneously - manage conservatively with analgesia ± medical expulsive therapy (alpha-blocker) and strain urine.
URGENT urology if obstruction WITH infection (obstructed infected system = emergency decompression), AKI, single kidney, or uncontrolled pain.
Larger/non-passing stones → urology for lithotripsy/ureteroscopy; advise hydration and prevention.

confirm: Sudden severe loin-to-groin colicky pain ± haematuria, restless patient; non-contrast CT KUB confirms a stone and its size/site.
disposition: Often outpatient; admit if infected/obstructed, AKI, or intractable pain.
